summary: Backend regression suite for the personal finance app. Executed 27 pytest tests covering seed defaults, dashboard aggregates, accounts, income/expense transactions, recurring commitments (12-month generation + cleanup on delete), installment purchases via both /installment-purchases and POST /transactions with payment_method=credito (no immediate expense tx, committed grows by total not per-month), overdue auto-marking, pay-commitment (creates expense, idempotent, no duplicate), split expenses (only my_share as expense, remainder as receivable), receive (creates income tx, partial->recebido transitions), loans borrowed (debts + commitments) and lent (receivables), needs realize flow, goals contribute, 365-day challenge toggle, planning (12 months), posso-comprar verdicts, reports shape, and full backup export/import/reset. All 27 tests PASSED against the public REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. Financial math (available = balance - committed, no duplicate lançamentos on pay/receive) verified correct.

minor.issue: Route signature uses `body: dict = None` (mutable/None default) — works but non-idiomatic FastAPI; Pydantic model preferred.
Accepts account_id as query param instead of body — inconsistent with other endpoints that use JSON bodies.
Accepts raw dict; no schema validation. Malformed payloads could partially wipe collections before failing.

critical_code_review_comments: engine.compute_planning: for month index i==0 the income logic mixes recurring vs realized in a convoluted way (`max(inc, realized_inc) if i==0 else inc` then re-overrides). Simplify — could double-count or drop income when both exist.

server.create_transaction: when installments>1 & type=expense, response schema differs from the normal path ({ok, type, purchase_id, installments} vs the tx doc). Consider consistent response shape for frontend consumers.

server.py: stamp() strips None values, but for updates PUT handlers use body.model_dump() with exclude None; consistent behavior — OK. However update_transaction uses TransactionUpdate but there's no way to null-out an existing field (e.g., remove a card_id).
engine.refresh_overdue mutates DB on every GET /commitments and GET /dashboard — could cause write pressure at scale; move to a scheduled task or debounce.
server.register_crud PUT accepts a raw dict for updates — bypasses Pydantic validation for accounts/cards/categories/people/goals/investments.
No unique/index constraints on `id` fields in MongoDB; risk of duplicate id if uuid collision or bad import.
compute_committed sums a_vencer + atrasado — matches expected behavior. Confirmed via tests.
Backup import replaces collections without transaction/rollback; a partial failure mid-loop leaves DB in inconsistent state.
seed_data_creation: Tests call DELETE /api/backup/reset at session start which reseeds default categories, Carteira account, and 365-day challenge. Test-created records are prefixed with TEST_.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run with: `cd /app && python -m pytest backend/tests/backend_test.py -v -n 0 --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/pytest_results.xml`. The pytest.ini enforces `-n 2 --dist loadscope` — you MUST override with `-n 0` for serial execution because tests share DB state via a session-scoped `ctx` fixture and rely on ordered execution (reset -> account -> tx -> recurring -> installment -> pay ...). xdist parallelism corrupts financial math assertions (e.g., committed=2400 instead of 1200 when installment-credit test races with recurring test). Suite is stable and fast (~7s).
rca of the issue: N/A - no functional bugs found. Only refactoring/code-quality suggestions above.
